newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CHEMICAL SECTOR SAYS GROWTH LIKELY TO SLOW.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CHEMICAL SECTOR SAYS GROWTH LIKELY TO SLOW.

text.p: Growth in the chemical industry is likely to slow after an impressive recovery last year, the Federation of Finnish Chemical Industries said in a report on Tuesday.

"The bottom of the recession for Finland's chemical industry was at the turn of 1995-1996, after which growth has been impressive ... at over nine percent adjusted for working days from December 1995 to December 1996," it said, referring to Statistics Finland data.
"Growth has been affected by extraordinary factors such as maintenance halts in the previous year and new capacity and it is likely that the pace will calm somewhat," it said.

But it said the international chemical industry lobby CEFIC's estimate for growth at three percent -- which refers mostly to base chemicals -- seemed slightly cautious in the light of new data and strong growth late last year.

In Finnish chemicals production, strong growth at the end of last year boosted this year's starting level and "since demand factors in exports and at home will develop favourably, maintaining this level or even raising it is possible," the federation said.
In Finnish chemical products, "a good demand trend is not necessarily seen in the sector's domestic production."
In Finnish plastics production, growth last year was so strong that it was unlikely to speed up but full-year growth would still be up on 1996, the federation said.
